start_here: Say to your AI: "Decide how many of the files sent with a message are accepted, and which limit stopped the rest, in words to show the person", with {"files":[{"name":"a.png","size":1000},{"name":"b.png","size":1000},{"name":"c.png","size":1000}],"limits":{"per_turn_cap":2}}. It runs tool:admit-attachments-to-a-message and answers {"accepted":[0,1],"left_out":[{"index":2,"because":"per_turn"}],"binding":"per_turn","banner":"Only the first 2 of 3 files were attached: one message holds up to 2.","blocked":false}
no_lists_because: It names no list of yours: it takes its input and answers, and keeps no row.
instructions: 1. Say to your AI: "Decide how many of the files sent with a message are accepted, and which limit stopped the rest, in words to show the person", and give it files.
2. The AI calls run_resource_operation at @workshop-tools with method tools:run, tool tool:admit-attachments-to-a-message and its input (the worked example shows one).

3. Read what comes back: Give files ([{ name, size }] in the order offered), and when wanted limits ({ per_turn_cap, absolute_bytes, max_bytes, binding_words }; defaults from src/attachment-admission.json), daily ({ remaining, resets_at } when the plan keeps a daily count) and now (milliseconds).
